scope: Secrets exposed through Git publication or outbound network traffic. UI and same-machine access issues are excluded from the conclusions at the operator's request.

conclusion.summary: Historical receipts show 2,304 successful FTP operations with TLS disabled and public-IP destinations across two real Accounts. SMTP TLS also fails to verify server certificates in both inspected connector versions. No real committed credential was confirmed in local or freshly fetched remote Git history.

findings.type: active configuration and recorded external transmission
findings.title: Two FTP Accounts send authentication over unencrypted FTP
evidence: Stored action receipts independently contain tls_mode=none, a literal public-IP host, and success status; conclusion does not rely solely on current configuration.
stackos_connectors/connectors/ftp/integration.py:223-234 selects ftplib.FTP for tls_mode=none, connects, and calls login(username, password).
Successful Account test receipts also retain tls_mode=none.
findings.impact: FTP authentication and transferred data lack application-level transport encryption. A network observer can capture credentials and contents.
findings.limits: No packet capture or evidence of interception was found. An external VPN or other network encapsulation cannot be established from these records. Hostnames, IPs and password values are omitted.
findings.remediation: Move both Accounts to verified FTPS, or SFTP where supported by both server and client. Verify secure transport, then rotate both FTP passwords. Avoid using the plaintext Accounts until transport is secured.

findings.type: code vulnerability with an active affected SMTP configuration
findings.title: SMTP TLS does not validate certificates or hostnames
evidence: Both Account tests and mail sending call SMTP_SSL or starttls without supplying a verified SSLContext.
No-network inspection of the local Python implementation confirmed CERT_NONE and check_hostname=False.
Installed desktop Python smtplib.py:778,1020 selects ssl._create_stdlib_context; its ssl.py:732-733,791 defines the unverified defaults.
The local repository pins 0.1.1; freshly fetched remote main pins 0.2.8, and the installed desktop 0.2.8 copy has the same flaw.
Read-only Account configuration review found an active SMTP Account using STARTTLS.
findings.impact: An attacker controlling the network path or SMTP DNS destination can impersonate the server with an untrusted certificate and receive the SMTP password and message content.
findings.limits: This confirms a vulnerability, not an observed interception. No real credential was used in a network test.
findings.remediation: Fix the canonical stackos-connectors SMTP transport to pass ssl.create_default_context() to SMTP_SSL and starttls on every probe/send path, including fallbacks. Add untrusted-certificate and hostname-mismatch regressions, publish the fixed package, and update the repository and desktop dependency. Updating only to inspected version 0.2.8 does not fix this.

git_scan.method: Local custom scanner using provider-token, private-key and credential-assignment patterns, with candidate triage and fingerprint-only reporting. Dedicated gitleaks/trufflehog/detect-secrets binaries were unavailable.
git_scan.commit_inventory_note: The initial local pass saw 1,352 commit objects. Two additional local commit objects appeared between scan stages; the final combined commit/tag pass covered both and all 43 remotely added commits. Their origin was not established.
git_scan.coverage: All original local objects, including unreachable objects and reflog history, plus newly fetched remote branch and tag objects.
git_scan.result: No real credential confirmed. High-signal matches were fixtures, examples or nonsecret identifiers. Historical secret-store filename inventory found only versions of website/.env.example; no seed.bin, auth.token, real .env, private-key files, database stores or obvious backup archives.
git_scan.limits: Does not inspect other repositories, forks, hidden pull-request refs, external CI logs or hosted release archives; pattern scanning cannot prove absence of every arbitrary or transformed secret. Credentials were not tested against providers.

local_scan.sqlite_result: No confirmed plaintext provider keys or private keys in the high-confidence pattern scan. Ciphertext BLOBs were not decrypted. Generic unlabeled passwords are not ruled out.
local_scan.other_network_configuration_result: No non-loopback http:// URLs in inspected nonrevoked Account configurations. IMAP uses SSL to loopback. FTP and IMAP verified TLS paths explicitly create verified SSL contexts.
exclusions: 19 archives or vendor executables larger than 25 MiB
non_internet_observations: Six complete Stripe S3 signed download URLs were retained in local httpx INFO logs. All had 600-second lifetimes and expired between 2026-09-23 and 2026-10-14. No tracked or published copies were found. This is local sensitive-data retention, not evidence of external disclosure.
Ignored .env.local contains signing configuration and a private-key path, not embedded private-key material.
Two ignored Nuxt-generated runtime security secrets had no exact copies in 36,919 inspected public-build/report files.

Vendored gstack includes Excalidraw client-side Firebase configuration with a Google-shaped API key. This is vendor client configuration rather than a StackOS/user provider credential; key restrictions were not tested.

verification.failure: test_oauth_lifecycle.py::test_required_scopes_are_checked_before_credential_use expects a later missing-scopes error; current code correctly rejects the request earlier through Search Console access_mode. Not evidence of an authorization bypass.

remediation_order: Stop plaintext FTP use, establish verified secure transport for both named Accounts, then rotate their passwords.
Correct SMTP certificate and hostname verification in the connector package and ship it to the desktop runtime.
Prevent complete signed URLs from entering local HTTP logs and enable repeatable secret scanning before publication.
